  • ncluding Remark
  • have seen:
  • in the manuscript of the ĪPK preserved in Lucknow, a number of
  • cerpts from the ĪPViv are found;
  • new fragments of the ĪPViv are found;
  • they are mainly from the avataraṇikā of the ĪPViv to the ĪPK; and
  • with reference to the part of the ĪPViv edited by Torella, the
  • agments of this manuscript give not only the avataraṇikā but also part
  • the commentary for the ĪPK and ĪPVr̥.
  • is true that a part of the text of the ĪPViv has been transmitted in
  • rth Indian manuscripts, but it is unlikely that the full text of the
  • Viv has been transmitted there. At least, the scribe of this
  • nuscript did not have it. For, if he had known of it, he would have
  • ven the part of the commentary for the ĪPK as well as the avataraṇikā
  • the ĪPViv with reference to the part of the ĪPViv which are not
  • ited.
  • vertheless, what is important here is that we can glean the new
  • agments of the ĪPViv from this manuscript. We should notice the
  • rginal notes of this manuscript not only from the aspect of gleaning
  • em but also from the aspect of the manuscript transmission of the
  • atyabhijñā texts. It is urgent that we should examine the rest of the
  • rginal notes in this manuscript.
